findings.detail: The rank-based binning assigns different bins to equal metric values, so equal repeat propensity or p values can receive arbitrary, item-order-dependent suffixes. This is not value-based quantile binning and manufactures distinctions unsupported by the specified demand metrics. The same issue affects the frequency deciles at lines 33-37 when equal counts straddle a rank boundary.
findings.reproduction: Use 3 training items, each with a single occurrence by a distinct user. They all have count=1, r=0, and p=0. Stable ranking assigns their repeat bins 0, 1, and 2 and their p bins 0 and 1; resulting suffixes differ despite identical statistics. Reordering the input item IDs can change which item receives each suffix.
findings.correction: Fit value thresholds/quantiles on training observations and assign equal values consistently (document a tie policy); do not split ties by stable item rank. Apply the same tie-consistent policy to frequency-decile assignment. Keep the fitted boundaries fixed for subsequent data.
